picks.title: Natsume Yuujinchou
picks.case: You gave Mushishi a 10, and this is the other great episodic series about a quiet person walking into somebody else's small supernatural problem and leaving it a little better. It asks for thirteen episodes and no commitment beyond one at a time, which answers the not-too-long half of what you asked for. Where Mushishi keeps Ginko at arm's length, Natsume lets its lead have friends, so it is the warmer of the two.

picks.title: Odd Taxi
picks.case: Monster is a 9 on your list, and this is the same pleasure — an ensemble of apparently unrelated people whose connections tighten every episode — compressed into thirteen. Almost all of it is conversations in a car, so the contemplative pace you asked for is structural rather than decorative. It also has the clean, deliberate ending that Bleach never got round to.

picks.title: Kino no Tabi
picks.case: Structurally this is the closest thing in the pool to Mushishi: a traveller arrives, observes one self-contained strangeness, and declines to fix it. It is colder than Natsume Yuujinchou and considerably less consoling, but it shares the refusal to hurry that made Mushishi work for you. Thirteen self-contained episodes.

picks.title: Sonny Boy
picks.case: Given Steins;Gate at an 8, you can sit with a series that withholds its rules for a long time. Sonny Boy is the most formally adventurous thing here and it uses that freedom to ask what a group of teenagers owes each other, in twelve episodes and without explaining itself. If Cowboy Bebop earned its 9 partly on atmosphere, this trades on the same account.
